title: Ignition Failure Lockout
shortDescription: Jandy heater failed to ignite the gas burner after multiple attempts and has locked out.
fullDescription:
The IFL (Ignition Failure Lockout) code on Jandy Lite2/LXi/JXi/LRZ heaters indicates the control board made the allowed number of ignition attempts without detecting a flame. The heater locks out for safety and stops all ignition attempts.

Common causes include an empty propane tank, closed gas valve, dirty flame sensor, weak spark from the igniter, or air trapped in the gas line after service. Wind gusts and cracked heat exchangers can also blow out the flame.

Clear the lockout by cycling power at the breaker, then troubleshoot upstream. If the heater re-locks after one or two cycles, call a pool professional — do not keep resetting a gas appliance.

causes.cause: Gas supply off, low propane, or closed valve
Dirty or carbon-coated flame sensor rod
Weak igniter or HSI (hot surface igniter) failure
Air in gas line after service
Control board or gas valve failure

fixSteps.title: Verify gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm propane tank is not empty and main gas valve is open. Light another gas appliance to confirm pressure.

fixSteps.title: Reset the heater
fixSteps.instruction: Turn heater off at breaker for 60 seconds, restore power, and call for heat.

fixSteps.title: Clean flame sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove flame sensor rod and gently polish with fine emery cloth. Reinstall.

whenToCallPro: If IFL recurs after cleaning or the gas valve needs replacement, call a licensed gas technician.

faq.q: How do I clear an IFL code?
faq.a: Shut the heater breaker off for one minute, then back on. If IFL returns, troubleshoot gas and flame sensor.

title: Stack Flue Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The stack flue sensor detects an abnormal flue temperature or is open/shorted.
fullDescription:
The SF code on Jandy JXi and LXi heaters indicates a problem with the stack flue sensor which monitors exhaust temperature inside the flue collector.

A dirty or sooted heat exchanger can produce high flue temperatures and trip this code. Rodent nests and obstructed vents are also common. An unplugged or damaged sensor harness will trigger SF immediately at startup.

Do not bypass the sensor — high flue temperatures indicate poor combustion or a blocked exchanger that can lead to a fire.

fixSteps.title: Inspect flue opening
fixSteps.instruction: With heater off and cool, check flue collector for obstructions, nests, or heavy soot.

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open the control panel and confirm the stack sensor two-pin connector is seated.

whenToCallPro: Heat exchanger cleaning or replacement must be done by a qualified tech.

title: Air Flow Switch Open
shortDescription: The combustion blower air flow switch did not close — insufficient airflow detected.
fullDescription:
AFS indicates the pressure switch on the combustion air blower has not closed, meaning the control board can't confirm that air is moving through the burner.

Typical causes include a failed blower motor, clogged blower wheel, a disconnected pressure tube, or an actual switch failure. Strong wind at the vent can also trip this switch momentarily.

This is a safety interlock — never bypass it, as insufficient combustion air produces carbon monoxide.

causes.cause: Cracked or pinched pressure tubing to AFS

symptoms: Blower runs but heater won't fire

fixSteps.title: Listen for blower startup
fixSteps.instruction: On a heat call, verify the combustion blower spins up within 2-3 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pressure tube
fixSteps.instruction: Trace the small silicone tube from blower to AFS; replace if cracked or pinched.

whenToCallPro: Blower replacement and draft pressure testing require a pro.
videoSearchQuery: Jandy JXi AFS air flow switch error

faq.a: Yes — gusty wind can briefly open the switch; if persistent, install a wind guard.

title: Water Pressure Switch Open
shortDescription: Heater does not detect sufficient water flow through the heat exchanger.
fullDescription:
The PS code means the water pressure switch has not closed, so the heater will not fire. Jandy heaters require a minimum flow (typically 25-30 GPM) through the exchanger.

Causes include a pump that isn't running, closed valves, clogged skimmer/pump baskets, a dirty filter, or an air-locked pump. A worn-out pressure switch itself can also be the culprit, especially after winterization.

Fire without flow will crack the heat exchanger within seconds, so the switch is critical.

causes.cause: Pool pump off or running slow (VS speed too low)
Closed valve in the return loop

fixSteps.title: Confirm pump priming
fixSteps.instruction: Verify pump is primed, basket clean, and running at heating-mode speed (usually 2600+ RPM for VS pumps).

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Backwash sand filter or rinse cartridge if pressure is more than 8 PSI above clean baseline.

whenToCallPro: If all flow is confirmed and PS remains, have a tech bench-test the switch.
videoSearchQuery: Jandy heater PS pressure switch error

faq.a: Switches can stick when dry — cycling the pump usually reseats them.

title: High Limit Switch Trip
shortDescription: Internal high-limit switch opened due to excessive water or exchanger temperature.
fullDescription:
HLF indicates one of the heater's high limit thermal fuses has tripped, usually because water temperature at the exchanger exceeded the 135°F safety threshold.

Scale build-up inside the copper tubes, low flow, or a stuck gas valve that continues firing after setpoint are typical causes. Repeated HLF trips point to a scaled or partially blocked exchanger.

Limits sometimes reset themselves after cooling; resetting power clears the code display.
symptoms: Heater shut down at normal setpoint

fixSteps.title: Restore full flow
fixSteps.instruction: Clean baskets and filter; increase pump speed.

whenToCallPro: De-scaling the heat exchanger is a professional job requiring acid flush.
videoSearchQuery: Jandy JXi HLF high limit fault

title: Water Temperature Sensor Open
shortDescription: Heater cannot read water inlet/outlet temperature — sensor open or disconnected.
fullDescription:
The WSB code is raised when the inlet or outlet thermistor is reading out of range (open circuit typically > 200kΩ). Without a valid water temperature reading, the heater cannot regulate output.

Corroded thermistor pins, rodent-chewed wiring, and board connector backouts are the usual suspects. The part itself is inexpensive but located in a tight well.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and replug the water temperature sensor connectors on the control board.

whenToCallPro: Sensor well leaks require proper sealing — call a pro if water drips.

title: VS FloPro Pump Drive Fault
shortDescription: Jandy VS FloPro variable speed pump drive detected an overcurrent or fault condition.
fullDescription:
The Drive Error on Jandy VSFHP and ePump series pumps indicates the drive electronics have detected a fault such as overcurrent, overtemperature, or phase imbalance and have shut the pump down.

Causes range from debris in the impeller, seized bearings, to electrical supply issues. Extreme ambient temperatures in the pump enclosure can also trip the overtemp protection.

Power-cycle to clear, but repeat faults mean the pump needs service.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off pump breaker for 60 seconds, restart.

fixSteps.title: Inspect impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Close valves, remove pump housing, check impeller for debris.

whenToCallPro: Drive replacement and bearing work require a pool technician.

faq.a: If out of warranty and pump is 8+ years old, replacement often wins on cost.

title: AquaLink Communication Fault
shortDescription: Jandy heater lost communication with AquaLink or iAquaLink automation panel.
fullDescription:
CF indicates the RS-485 bus between the AquaLink controller and the heater has failed. The heater will still operate via its local keypad but cannot be controlled by automation until communication is restored.

Chewed control cables, loose 4-pin terminals inside the heater, or a failed RS-485 interface on the board are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Check bus wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Open heater terminal block, verify the red/black/yellow/green 4-pin connector is tight.

faq.a: Yes — you can operate via its own keypad in Spa/Pool mode.

title: Header Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The heat exchanger header sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
HS on Jandy heaters indicates the thermistor mounted in the front header is reading an invalid value. This sensor protects the exchanger by shutting down the burner if local water temperature spikes.

A dried-out O-ring, mineral scale, or broken lead wire are typical culprits.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug header sensor, measure resistance (~10kΩ at 77°F). Replace if open/shorted.

whenToCallPro: If you suspect scaled exchanger, call a pro for descaling.

faq.q: Can I swap inlet and header sensors?
faq.a: They are different part numbers — match by Jandy part list.

title: ePump Overcurrent Fault
shortDescription: Jandy ePump drive has detected an overcurrent condition on the motor output.
fullDescription:
E05 on the Jandy ePump indicates the drive shut down because motor current exceeded safe limits. The pump is usually trying to turn a blocked impeller, or the motor windings have partially shorted.

Debris removal clears most E05s. Recurring faults point to motor failure.
symptoms: Pump trips at high RPM only

fixSteps.title: Clear impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Isolate pump, remove housing, pull impeller free of debris.

whenToCallPro: Motor or drive replacement requires a pool tech.

faq.a: Temporarily yes, but it only masks the underlying fault.
